pass_a_gloss:
As balls they will be thrown, having fallen from their own container that held them. Solomon says something like this: 'As a bird when it falls from its own nest, so a man when he is torn from his own places.' What could be more pitiful than those in captivity? What is more lamentable and trodden down than humans falling under the hand of their conquerors? It happened in the days of Ahaz, son of Joatham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but they could not besiege it. Those who reject the historical narrative in the divinely inspired Scriptures, flee, as it seems, from understanding the things written in them in the proper way. Spiritual theory is good and profitable, and it enlightens the eye of the mind, making it most intelligent. When something from the historical events is brought to us through the sacred Scriptures, then we should seek the useful thing from history, so that the divinely inspired Scripture may appear to us as saving and beneficial from all sides. The prophetic word tells us what happened during the reign of Uzziah to those from Judah and Benjamin, and to the ten tribes in Samaria, who were also called Ephraim and Israel.

Since in the times of four kings the entire word of prophecy occurred, the prophet sets forth the events happening in each time and necessarily indicates the order of the visions or his own words, assigning the best order. After Azariah and Uzziah died, Jotham succeeded to the kingdom and followed the purpose and pursuits of his own father. For he is said to have done what is right in the eyes of the Lord, just like Uzziah, except he did not remove the high places, but the people still burned incense on the high places. Uzziah had sought to offer sacrifices to God and burn incense, and had been rebuked for this reason. Jotham, however, did not do so. After he died, Ahaz succeeded to the kingdom, during the reign of Pekah son of Remaliah over Israel, that is, the twelve tribes. This man waged war against Ahaz and Judah and killed one hundred twenty thousand in one day. For the God of all was provoking Ahaz in his impieties, about which it is written in the fourth book of Kings that he walked in the way of the king of Israel. For he was an impious man and had served idols, and had passed his children through fire, sacrificing to the unclean demons.
pass_b_english: The people will lie helpless, like walnuts that have fallen from their container, a situation that Solomon describes by comparing a bird that has fallen from its nest to a person who has been torn from their own place, saying, 'As a bird when it falls from its own nest, so a man when he is torn from his own places' (Proverbs 27:8), which highlights the pitiful state of those in captivity, who are trodden down and helpless under the power of their conquerors.

This plight is vividly illustrated in the historical narrative of the Scriptures, which tells us that during the reign of Ahaz, son of Joatham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, waged war against Jerusalem, but were unable to besiege it.

It seems that those who reject the historical narrative in the divinely inspired Scriptures flee from understanding the things written in them in the proper way, which is a shame, because spiritual theory, which is good and profitable, enlightens the eye of the mind, making it most intelligent.

When something from the historical events is brought to us through the sacred Scriptures, then we should seek the useful thing from history, so that the divinely inspired Scripture may appear to us as saving and beneficial from all sides, providing valuable insights and lessons.

The prophetic word sheds light on the events that occurred during the reign of Uzziah, affecting not only the tribes of Judah and Benjamin but also the ten tribes in Samaria, who were also called Ephraim and Israel.

Since the entire word of prophecy occurred during the times of four kings, the prophet sets forth the events happening in each time, indicating the order of the visions or his own words and assigning the best order.

After Azariah and Uzziah died, Jotham succeeded to the kingdom and followed the purpose and pursuits of his own father, doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord, just like Uzziah, except he did not remove the high places, but the people still burned incense on the high places.
Unlike Uzziah, who had sought to offer sacrifices to God and burn incense, and had been rebuked for this reason, Jotham did not attempt to do so.

After he died, Ahaz succeeded to the kingdom, during the reign of Pekah, son of Remaliah, over Israel, that is, the twelve tribes, and this man waged war against Ahaz and Judah, killing one hundred twenty thousand in one day.

The God of all was provoking Ahaz in his impieties, about which it is written in the fourth book of Kings that he walked in the way of the king of Israel (2 Kings 16:3), serving idols and passing his children through fire, sacrificing to the unclean demons.
